title: CMU 15-445: Database Systems — Software Engineering Kickoff

unit.title: Engineering a Small, Testable Buffer Pool
unit.audience: A learner strong in data structures and algorithms who is building C++ software-engineering practice.
learning_objectives: Turn an informal systems idea into an explicit C++ component contract.
Implement deterministic fixed-capacity residency, pinning, LRU replacement, dirty-page write-back, and error handling.
Protect component invariants across ordinary and failure paths.
Build repeatable tests with a controllable storage test double and document engineering trade-offs.
Reason about ownership, observable state, complexity, and future concurrency hazards.
scope_in: A standalone C++17 in-memory buffer-pool model
An injected page-store boundary and deterministic failure injection
Dirty tracking, explicit flush, and write-back before eviction
Automated tests, reproducible build commands, and concise design notes
scope_out: The official CMU 15-445 Project #1 specification or starter code
The complete BusTub buffer pool manager
Concurrency control, background flushing, real disk I/O, B+ trees, SQL execution, and query optimization
Any claim of completing CMU 15-445 or its assignments

requires_all: All expected submission evidence is present and attributable to this attempt.
The documented build and test commands succeed in the validation environment.
Independent tests confirm the required behavior and invariant preservation.
An examiner applies examiner_only/RUBRIC.md and records a passing result.
